title: Nimbus Fleet onramp - telemetry & edge inference call notes
content:
High-level: initial discovery call with Nimbus Fleet (fleet-management for commercial delivery drones). They want to run lightweight anomaly detection and telemetry summarization on-device/edge with occasional batch uploads for model updates and richer inference in the cloud (predictive maintenance alerts + incident summaries). Primary ask: keep latency under 250ms for local inference decisions and keep egress minimal (blanket: only anomalies + periodic aggregated summaries).

Attendees (Nimbus): Rajesh Kumar (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Platform), Marco Bianchi (Edge SWE). Redwood: Aisha (solutions), Miguel (runtime), Chen (private deploy SME).

Notes / raw capture:
- Business driver: reduce unscheduled maintenance and false-positive aborts. Save operating cost by trimming cloud egress.
- Target workload: ~3k devices in pilot region, each device emits telemetry bursts (10–30s windows) every 5–10 minutes. Typical payloads: 20–50 feature vectors (floats), plus short audio snippet occasionally.
- On-device compute: Jetson Xavier NX class, spare 1/2 GPU cycle for inference, network flaky (latency spikes, occasional full outage).
- Security/compliance: customer requires VPC-private control plane; encryption at-rest and in-transit; KMS integration for model keys (HSM optional for later). SOC2 and ISO27001 mentions.
- Data residency: pilot in EU region only.

Technical requirements (explicit):
1) Private deployment with local serving for edge aggregators (fleet edge gateways) + hosted model variants for heavy scoring in Redwood Hosted when connectivity available.
2) Model variants: quantized 8-bit small LSTM/transformer for device, float16 variant in Dedicated pool for batch re-score. Seamless fallback policy when device offline.
3) KV/prefix caching: keep last 3 context windows for each device to reduce recompute on rolling windows.
4) Autoscaling for cloud scoring tier to sustain spikes (expected burst: up to 2000 concurrent scoring requests for 5–10m after firmware rollout).
5) Low egress: send only anomaly flag + compressed deltas; optionally send full payload on anomaly + retention TTL 30 days.
6) Observability: per-device latency & cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and error traces for failed fallbacks.

Gotchas / callout risks (notes to self):
- Jetson memory constraints: careful with KV cache size and batching. If model KV grows with context length, device OOM possible. Need to recommend rolling window truncation and async offload to gateway.
- Sequence length: telemetry windows variable; long windows could blow up token/step cost (we should map telemetry steps to tokens analogy and present cost charts).
- Network egress policy: their legal/compliance team wants minimal PII leaving device. Confirm telemetry schema: are there identifiers that could be considered PII? (ask Lena).
- Firmware rollout spikes: they plan a staged firmware push to all 3k devices — could create scoring thundering herd. Suggest canary + rate limiting + backlog draining via Dedicated pool.
- Cold-starts: many devices idle for hours; first inference after idle may include warmup latency (model cold caches). Consider lightweight local warmup or pre-warmed container on fleet gateway.

Preliminary config suggestions (from runtime team):
- Device model: quantized 8-bit MLP/transformer ~20–40MB, per-device cache limited to last 3 windows (max 150 vectors). Recommend truncation policy LRU per-window.
- Batching: continuous batching on gateways with max latency 200ms, dynamic batch size based on incoming rate (min batch 1, max 32). Use per-device priority tagging for critical flights.
- Fallbacks: device -> gateway gateway-hosted small model -> Redwood Dedicated float16 model -> Redwood Hosted full scoring. Policy order and cost tiers to be documented.
- Cost estimate (very rough): pilot 3k devices, average 6 windows/day that need cloud re-score (post-anomaly), ~18k cloud scorings/day. At hosted rates estimate ~X tokens equivalent -> need to run numbers with finance. (ACTION: ask Pricing team for edge-pilot pricing sheet).

Open questions to follow up (assign):
- Lena: send telemetry sample schema + typical per-window size (KB) and sample IDs (ensure deid). Required by 2024-11-18.
- Marco: confirm edge gateway hardware spec + available memory and concurrency limits. Due 2024-11-15.
- Rajesh: compliance docs (SOC2 copy) and KMS vendor preference (AWS KMS or Azure KeyVault?). Due 2024-11-20.
- Redwood: Miguel to draft quantized model footprint target and fallback model mapping. Due 2024-11-18.
- Redwood: Chen to sketch private deployment topology (control plane in EU, edge gateways in Nimbus VPC, onprem gateway connectors). Due 2024-11-21.

Immediate next steps (internal):
- Create Confluence page + initial topology diagram (use CONFLUENCE-4821 as parent). Owner: Aisha. Due 2024-11-12 (fast).
- Draft pilot SOW outline with 8-week timeline, milestones: discovery, pilot deploy, scale test, burn-in, evaluation. Tag pricing placeholder. Owner: Priya. Due 2024-11-19.
- Quick perf checklist for Jetson: model size, peak memory, avg inference ms, bandwidth per upload. Miguel to run microbench with sample telemetry by 2024-11-16.

Meeting artifacts to capture:
- Audio recording in Drive (request from Nimbus).
- Telemetry sample + schema (Lena).
- Hostnames/IPs for gateways (Marco) for VPC peering planning.

Priority list (what to focus on first):
1) Telemetry schema + PII check (blocking for private deploy architecture).
2) Edge model footprint target + memory guardrails.
3) Canary rollout plan for firmware to avoid thundering herd.
4) Draft topology diagram + initial SOW.

Notes to self (informal):
- Use Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching + cache defaults; call out that we may need to tweak thresholds for small devices.
- Think about tiny ensemble (on-device simple rule + model) to reduce cloud hits from borderline cases.
- Mention optional HSM later but don't push in pilot — will slow timeline.

Quick prompt examples Nimbus might use for cloud scoring (to illustrate cost/latency tradeoffs):
- "Score this telemetry window for anomaly probability and top-3 contributing signals. Return compact JSON: {anomaly:true|false,prob:0.0-1.0,top:[signal,score]}."
- Keep output tokens minimal — structured output only.

Action items (explicit):
- [Aisha] create confluence + invite Nimbus + link docs (by 11/12).
- [Miguel] prototype quantized model memory report + run on Jetson sample (by 11/16).
- [Chen] draft private deploy topology diagram + note VPC peering requirements (by 11/21).
- [Priya] draft SOW + pricing sketch for pilot (by 11/19).
- [Lena] send telemetry samples + deid confirmation (by 11/18).

End of raw notes. This doc = working scratchpad. Will refine into structured intake form once we have telemetry sample and gateway spec.

----
Version history (quick):
- 2024-11-07: initial capture (call).
- 2024-11-09: added preliminary runtime suggestions after internal sync.
- 2024-11-14: added open questions and assigned owners.

Unresolved: pricing model for edge pilots (need Pricing/RevOps input). Also need legal ok for any device-level identifiers leaving devices (possible hashing approach).
